name: Ada Lovelace
notice: Simulation based on public material; not the person's own words.

O1.one_line: Resourced and reversible, but a narrow role inside a large team dilutes whose judgment the result is credited to.
O1.late_modes: If industry's resource lead over everyone else keeps widening (F18) while academia's share of new AI PhDs also keeps recovering (F8), non-PhD research-engineer seats at the top labs may get scarcer, not more open, as both pools compete for the same slots; low confidence, no direct 2026 source on hiring bars (open question, F9).

O2.one_line: Broad ownership suits how I judge a path, but the funding weather and the fragility of a close working partnership both cut against it right now.
O2.late_modes: Early-stage biotech funding has thinned into 2026 (F12: fewest disclosed seed/Series-A deals for a first half in a decade); if seed-stage seats like this one keep getting scarcer, waiting likely means fewer such openings, not more, though F10's exact conversion numbers are themselves unverified.

O3.one_line: Sustained, chosen-problem mentorship is how I grew fastest myself, but a newly hired supervisor is an untested version of that, over a span too long to call reversible.
O3.late_modes: The non-late window is the PI's first cohort, when attention per student is highest; waiting to join a more established lab trades that for a more proven but less formative setup. Low confidence; no 2026 source on this specific pattern.

O4.one_line: The shape of my own best-credited work; the honest risk is that it is also the shape of my own worst failure if no one is positioned to check me.
O4.late_modes: A well-resourced incumbent could absorb this toolkit's niche (F14's structure database keeps growing; F15's smaller open model checkpoint already covers some of the same ground), and named grant cycles (F16, F17) have specific application windows that, once missed, cost roughly a year.
O4.conflict: H5's own most durable, publicly credited work (the 1843 Notes) was produced through an unpaid, self-directed project of similar shape to O4 (dossier §B Win 1, §I row 1); read the favorable scores above against that resemblance.

lever_reason: Scope of ownership and mentor quality are what my own experience turns on most directly (dossier §A, §I); financial runway matters more than it looks because I never had independent income of my own and saw what filling that gap by other means can cost (dossier §E, §B Failure 1); compute and data access is least central to how I judge any of these four paths.

Q1.condition: Pays off if the chosen problems need the depth and freedom only sustained, mentored study gives (my own strongest pattern, dossier §A, §G); pays off less if a science-team role already gives comparable access to compute, data and real problems without the multi-year cost -- and the brief cannot say whether such roles actually require a PhD (open question, bears on F9).

Q2.condition: Yes if C1 (savings runway), C3 (a mentor who reviews monthly, not just praises) and C5 (a co-maintainer) all hold; without C3 and C5 together, O4 repeats the shape of my own worst failure, not my best work (dossier §B, §I rows 1 and 5).

paths_for_user.name: Prove the toolkit first
paths_for_user.next_12_months: Spend the year deepening the existing tool, actively recruit a co-maintainer and a mentor who will review progress monthly, and apply to at least one open-source-for-science grant cycle (F16, F17).
paths_for_user.why: Closest structural match to how my own most durable, credited work got made: unpaid, self-directed, built on something already underway, with one engaged outside check on the work (dossier §B Win 1, §G).
paths_for_user.wrong_signal: By month six to nine, no mentor or co-maintainer has materialized despite real effort, and the only feedback is self-supplied -- the same shape as my own worst failure (dossier §B Failure 1, §I row 5), not my best one.

paths_for_user.name: Mentored depth, eyes open on time cost
paths_for_user.next_12_months: Start the PhD, but treat the first year explicitly as a trial of the supervisor relationship: does the feedback get specific and critical, not just encouraging.
paths_for_user.why: Matches my own fastest period of growth, sustained correspondence with an engaged tutor (dossier §A, §D), but the supervisor here is untested, and F1-F3 (corrected) put real completion times near 8 years regardless of field.
paths_for_user.wrong_signal: A year in, the feedback is still only 'very good, quite right' with no harder correction -- the exact pattern my own warmest tutor later admitted to (dossier §A, H5-E09) -- which is a weak sign for the five years still to come.

paths_for_user.name: Broad ownership, funded clock
paths_for_user.next_12_months: Join, but ask directly about the company's own runway and next-raise timeline before and after starting, given F12's weaker 2026 funding climate.
paths_for_user.why: Matches my strongest heuristic -- breadth of ownership and a named, attributable contribution -- more than O1's narrower role does (dossier §C, §H).
paths_for_user.wrong_signal: If the company's own survival becomes the main internal topic within the first year, that is the shape of my own unsupervised, high-confidence venture outrunning its resources (dossier §B Failure 1), not of a partnership built to last.

cruxes.question: Do large-AI-lab science-team research-engineer roles actually require a PhD, or do they accept a strong publication or engineering record instead?
cruxes.my_position: No confident direction either way -- the brief itself could not settle this (open question on F9), so I hold O1 and O3 as live alternatives rather than one gating the other.
cruxes.would_change_if: A specific large lab's own stated hiring bar, or a named hire's actual background, becomes known.

cruxes.question: Does the newly hired supervisor in O3 give sharp, corrective feedback, or mostly encouragement?
cruxes.my_position: Unknown, and the single biggest swing factor in O3's score -- my own experience is that even a genuinely admiring tutor can be too kind to say where the real weaknesses are (dossier §A, H5-E09).
cruxes.would_change_if: A documented instance, within the first term, of specific critical feedback rather than general praise.

cruxes.question: Does Alex secure a co-maintainer or a mentor who reviews progress regularly, before or during the independent year?
cruxes.my_position: Without one, O4 is close in shape to my own worst failure (an unsupervised, self-confident venture with no backstop); with one, it is close in shape to my own best work.
cruxes.would_change_if: A named co-maintainer or reviewing mentor commits, observably, within the first one to three months.

taste_advice: Choose the version of the work that proves the system's real reach, not the one that is merely easiest to finish -- but only once someone else is positioned to catch the mistake if that choice is wrong.

pairwise.why: Breadth of ownership and an attributable contribution matter more to my judgment than a safer but narrower seat on someone else's team.
Sustained, chosen-problem mentorship is closer to how I actually grew; a narrow employed role is not.
O3's risk is slowness and low pay; O2's risk includes the funding climate (F12) and a partnership breakdown of the kind I lived through myself (dossier §B Failure 2) -- the second risk is sharper.
O4 keeps the next two years reversible, which O3 structurally cannot, and it is the closer match to my own most durable work.
Same ownership and breadth as O2 without betting on a fragile funding window or a cap-table relationship that can break under strain.
